bug_semantics: In bgp_attr_nhc(), a crafted BGP UPDATE carrying a Next Hop Dependent Characteristics (NHC) attribute can underflow the remaining-length counter. Remaining NHC length is a uint16 bgp_size_t. The TLV loop reads the 4-byte TLV header (code+length = BGP_NHC_TLV_MIN_LEN) then checks only `if (length < tlv_length)` before later doing `length -= tlv_length + BGP_NHC_TLV_MIN_LEN`. When remaining length is in [tlv_length, tlv_length+3], the check passes and the unsigned subtract wraps (e.g. 5-6 -> 65535). The loop is `while (length && STREAM_READABLE(s) >= BGP_NHC_TLV_MIN_LEN)`, and STREAM_READABLE is the whole UPDATE stream, so a wrapped length keeps parsing subsequent UPDATE bytes as NHC TLVs (allocations/DoS). STREAM_READABLE < tlv_length can stop an over-read of the stream itself, but does not stop the underflow. CWE-191; unauthenticated remote DoS via BGP UPDATE.
flaw_origin: The incomplete remaining-length check was written with the original NHC parser, not by a later edit. d311a698deb84cf249fc1f258ce639d48565b110 (PR #18729) added static int bgp_attr_nhc() with both `if (length < tlv_length)` at bgpd/bgp_attr.c:3691 and `length -= tlv_length + BGP_NHC_TLV_MIN_LEN` at :3736. AIGP's similar `if (length < tlv_length)` at :519 is a different TLV format where length includes the header and is not this bug. Intermediate NHC edits through 2026-03-10 kept the broken predicate until the one-line fix.
